task_instruction:
Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		Your phone has been showing 'No Service' for the past few hours.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hi, I'm hoping you can help. My phone has been showing "No Service" for the past few hours and I can't seem to get a signal at all.

turns.thought:
I'm sorry to hear you're having service issues — let's get this sorted out. To start, I'll need to look up your account.

Could you please provide either:
- the **phone number** associated with your line, **or**
- your **full name and date of birth** so I can verify your identity?
turns.execution_output: User: Sure — my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002.

turns.thought: Found your account. Your line (555-123-2002) is currently **Suspended**, which is why you have no service. Let me check your bills to see what's causing it.

turns.thought:
I've found the cause of the problem. Your line **555-123-2002 (L1002)** is currently **suspended** — that's why you're seeing "No Service." The suspension was started today, 2025-02-25, because of an **overdue bill**.

Here's the bill:
- **Bill ID:** B1234321
- **Billing period:** 2025-01-01 to 2025-01-31
- **Amount due:** $65.00
- **Due date:** 2025-01-15 (now overdue)

Good news: your line's contract runs through 2026-12-31, so once this overdue bill is paid I can lift the suspension and restore your service.

To proceed, I'll send a payment request for this overdue bill to your line/account. Once it's sent, you'll need to check your payment request (via your check_payment_request tool) and accept it so I can process the payment. Shall I send the payment request now?
turns.execution_output: User: Yes, please go ahead and send the payment request. I'd like to get this resolved as soon as possible.
Payment request sent to the customer for bill B1234321

turns.thought:
Your payment request has been sent and bill B1234321 is now in **Awaiting Payment** status.

Please go ahead and:
1. **Check your payment request** using the `check_payment_request` tool on your device, and
2. **Accept it** so I can process the payment.

Let me know once you've accepted it (or if you run into any issues), and I'll take care of the payment and get your line restored right away.

Your line is restored:

- **Bill B1234321:** $65.00 — status is now **Paid**
- **Line 555-123-2002 (L1002):** status is now **Active**, suspension cleared

Please **reboot your device** now so it can reconnect to the network and pick up service. Once it restarts, you should see signal bars return.

One more thing to flag: you have another bill, **B1002** for $150.00 (period 2025-02-01 to 2025-02-28), currently issued and due **2025-02-19**. Would you like me to send a payment request for that one as well to keep your account in good standing?

That's actually a separate issue from the suspension — and an easy one to fix. Airplane Mode disables all wireless radios on your phone (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), so no signal bars can appear while it's on. Since your line is now Active, turning Airplane Mode off should bring your service right back.

Please do this on your device:

1. **Open your quick settings panel** by swiping down from the top of the screen.
2. **Tap the airplane icon (✈️)** to turn Airplane Mode **OFF**. The icon should no longer be highlighted.
   - Alternatively, go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Airplane Mode** and toggle it off.
3. Wait a few seconds and **check your status bar** again — you should now see signal bars along with the network type (e.g., 5G or LTE).

Let me know what your status bar shows once Airplane Mode is off. If signal bars are back, I'll send the payment request for bill B1002 ($150.00) right away. If you're still not seeing any signal, tell me exactly what's displayed and we'll keep troubleshooting (SIM status, APN settings, network mode preference, etc.).
I understand — let's work through this systematically. Let me check your device and plan details first.

I understand your frustration — you've done the right steps so far. Your line is confirmed Active on our end, so let's narrow this down on the device side.

Please go ahead and run these two checks on your phone, one at a time, and tell me exactly what each one reports:

1. **`check_sim_status()`** — this tells us whether your SIM is properly seated/active, or if it's showing missing or locked.
2. **`check_network_mode_preference()`** — this tells us what network technology your phone is set to prefer. If it's stuck on an older mode (2G/3G), it can prevent you from connecting.

While you do that, here's what I've confirmed from our side:
- Line **555-123-2002** is **Active** with no suspension.
- Your device (**Smartphone Pro Max**, IMEI ending 3456) is **activated**.
- Your plan (**Premium Plan**, 15 GB/month) is fine, and your usage is 8.7 GB — well under the limit, so this isn't a data cap issue.

Go ahead and send me those two results and we'll take the next step from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me run the first check for you.

turns.thought:
Good — that rules out a lot. Your SIM is fine and your network mode is set correctly, so we know the phone isn't misconfigured there.

The remaining likely culprit is the **"Data Disabled"** flag in your status bar, plus possibly your APN settings. Let's tackle these in order:

**Step 1 — Turn mobile data ON**

On your device, please use **`toggle_data()`** to switch mobile data ON.

- If you'd rather do it manually: **Settings → Network & Internet → Mobile Network**, and turn the **Mobile Data** toggle on.

**Step 2 — Check whether the signal returned**

Once data is enabled, tell me what your status bar shows. If you now see signal bars plus a network type (5G/LTE), we're back in business.

**Step 3 — If there's still no signal, check APN settings**

If you still have "No Signal," please run **`check_apn_settings()`** and tell me what it reports. Incorrect APN settings can cause a loss of service, and if they show as incorrect I'll have you run **`reset_apn_settings()`** followed by a **`reboot_device()`**, since the reset only takes effect after a restart.

Let me know what Step 1 and (if needed) Step 3 give you. Once your signal is back, I'll send that payment request for bill B1002 ($150.00) as you asked.

Yes — please go ahead. An APN name of "broken" definitely isn't right; valid APN settings are required to connect to our mobile data network, and this is very likely what's blocking your signal.

Please do it in this exact order, since the reset won't take effect until after the restart:

1. **Run `reset_apn_settings()`** on your device — this restores the APN to our correct default settings.
2. **Run `reboot_device()`** — this is required for the new APN settings to apply.
3. After the phone restarts, **check your status bar again** and tell me what you see (signal bars, network type, data status).

A quick note for later: your MMSC URL (`http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc`) is correctly set, so once the APN is restored, picture/video messaging should work as well.

Let me know what your status bar shows after the reboot. If you've got bars back, I'll immediately send the payment request for bill B1002 ($150.00), as you asked. And if you're still seeing "No Signal," we'll keep going — I haven't run out of things for us to try.
